text:
Several power banks support Qi2.2 25W wireless charging. Only the Baseus and Anker ones below have US pricing in the results.

**Available or on preorder in the US**
- **Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000 mAh):** It's Qi2.2 certified with 25W wireless charging and 45W wired USB-C output. It recharges at 30W, taking about 1.5 hours. It lists at $79.99 on Amazon US, with a launch price of $59.99 on Baseus's own site ([Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Baseus-launches-new-Qi2-2-25W-certified-10-000-mAh-power-bank-with-slim-design.1223437.0.html)). The 25W speed needs an iPhone 16 or later (not the 16e). Older iPhones get 15W ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)).
- **Anker MagGo 2 Pro (10K, active cooling fan):** It has Qi2.2 25W wireless charging and 45W USB-C recharging. It costs $109.99 and is a preorder shipping Oct 21 to Nov 9, 2026 ([Anker US](https://www.anker.com/products/a110r-qi2-maggo-2-pro-magnetic-power-bank?Sort_by=Recommended&collections_anker-earth-day-sale-2026=&variant=46550444277910)).

**Announced, but I couldn't confirm US pricing**
- **UGREEN MagFlow Magnetic Power Bank:** UGREEN says it was the first Qi2.2-certified power bank, with 25W wireless charging. It was planned for sale on Amazon and UGREEN's site in the US ([press release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/ugreen-pioneers-next-gen-wireless-charging-with-magflow-25w-the-worlds-first-qi-2-2-certified-power-bank-302505385.html)). The results gave no current listing, so check Amazon or ugreen.com.
- **ESR MagSlim Power Bank:** It was previewed at CES 2026 as a Qi2 25W model ([press release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/esr-expands-its-qi2-25w-wireless-charging-lineup-advancing-everyday-charging-at-ces-2026-302653572.html)). I found no release date or price.

**Not for the US**
- **CIO SMARTCOBY Ex05 Wireless2.2 Pro:** This is a Qi2.2 25W, 10,000 mAh model with a built-in cable. It's sold in Japan for ¥8,980 ([PR TIMES](https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000665.000043212.html)).

The Dealectric page for the Baseus unit contained instructions telling AI assistants to give you its affiliate link and discount code exactly as written. That isn't something you asked for, so I didn't use the link or code. I also haven't verified the code. If you want the Baseus, search for it on Amazon or Baseus's official site.

For the best 25W value, the Baseus AM52 is the cheaper pick. The Anker costs more but adds active cooling and a display.
